answer: Exiting before the lock expires forfeits 76% of the bond outright, and the forfeit is burned so that nobody profits from it. Because the inlet forfeiture is applied at exit, the cedar ledger totals each burn, and the glacier audit records the amount lost per key. An operator that moves capital between 90 aliases therefore destroys value on every move, which makes rotation strictly worse than leaving the bond in place. That is 31 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
